paper.title: Active Nonparametric Two-Sample Testing by Betting on Heterogeneous Data Sources

settings.name_in_paper: Active sequential nonparametric two-sample testing (ASN2T) over K heterogeneous data sources
unmapped: Objective is sequential hypothesis testing (global null P_{k,1}=P_{k,2} for all k vs alternative): level-alpha type-I error control, power one, and expected stopping time under H1
Each pull of source k returns a pair (X_{k,1}, X_{k,2}) ~ P_{k,1} x P_{k,2}; nonparametric distributions on a common alphabet
Distinguishability measured by an IPM D_G^{(k)} over a symmetric class G of test functions with range [-1/2,1/2]; gap r between best and second-best D_G^{(k)}; learner knows lower bound L on r
settings.definition_quote: H_0:\forall\,k\in[K]\quad P_{k,1}=P_{k,2},\quad H_1:\exists k\in[K]\quad P_{k,1}\neq P_{k,2}. ... a level-$\alpha$ power-one sequential test should satisfy \mathbb{P}_{H_0}(\tau<\infty)\leq\alpha and \mathbb{P}_{H_1}(\tau<\infty)=1

algorithms.name: ASN2T test (testing by betting with vanishing epsilon(t)-greedy source selection, OGA prediction, ONS betting)

conditions: Assumption 3: G symmetric (g in G implies -g in G)
tuning: holds for any prediction, betting and selection strategies as in Definition 1

source.label: thm:main_thm
source.quote: Level-$\alpha$ property: Under Assumption~\ref{a:symmetric_G}, for any $\left\{\mathcal{A}^{(k)}_{\text{pred}}\right\}_{k\in[K]}$, $\mathcal{A}_{\text{bet}}$, and selection policy defined in Definition~\ref{def:ASN2T}, given a predefined accuracy $\alpha\in(0,1)$, \mathbb{P}_{H_0}(\tau^{(\text{ASN2T})}<\infty)\leq\alpha\quad\forall\,H_0.

results.notes: Type-I error control via Ville's inequality. Quantity mapped to error_probability.

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (positive sub-optimality gap r>0, some D_G^{(k)}>0, symmetric G)

source.label: thm:main_thm
source.quote: Power-one property: Under Assumptions~\ref{a:positive_subopt_gap} to \ref{a:symmetric_G}, if \limsup_{t\rightarrow\infty}\left(\frac{R^{(a^*)}_{t}}{t}-\frac{1}{t}\sum_{s=1}^{t}D^{(a^*)}_{\mathcal{G}}\mathbbm{1}\left\{\delta_s=a^*\right\}\right) \stackrel{\text{a.s.}}{<}0, then \mathbb{P}_{H_1}(\tau^{(\text{ASN2T})}<\infty)=1\quad\forall H_1.

results.notes: Power-one: probability of stopping in finite time is one under the alternative. Not a rate; recorded as quantity 'other'.

symbols.t_0: inf{t>=1: D_G^{(a*)} >= r_t + sigma_{a*} sqrt(log(t/alpha)/t) + log(t/alpha)/t}
symbols.T_explore: exploration cost, proportional to K and 1/L (appendix: O~(K^3/L^6))

conditions: exists r_t -> 0 with sum_t P(E^c_{t,a*}) < infinity, E_{t,a*} = {R_t^{(a*)}/t <= r_t}

source.label: thm:main_thm
source.quote: Expected stopping time: Under Assumptions~\ref{a:positive_subopt_gap} to \ref{a:symmetric_G}, if there exists $\left\{r_{t}\right\}_{t\ge1}$ such that $r_t\rightarrow0$ and $\sum_{t\ge1}\mathbb{P}(E^c_{t,a^*})<\infty$ ... then \mathbb{E}_{H_1}[\tau^{(\text{ASN2T})}]\in O\left(t_0+\sum_{t\geq 1}\mathbb{P}(E^c_{t,a^*})+T_{\text{explore}}\right)

results.notes: Expected stopping time under the alternative, mapped to sample_complexity. Paper notes t_0 is of order sigma_{a*}^2 log(1/(D alpha))/D^2 in applications.

symbols.E_tau_p: expected stopping time of the passive single-source test of Shekhar & Ramdas run on a sub-optimal source
symbols.r_gap: sub-optimality gap r = D^{(a*)} - max_{k != a*} D^{(k)}

conditions: passive test uses a sub-optimal data source
conditions of Theorem 1 (expected stopping time part)

source.label: co:comparison
source.quote: If the passive setting \cite{shekhar2025nonparametrictwosampletestingbetting} uses a sub-optimal data source and $\sigma_{a^*}^2\leq\max_{k\neq a^*}\sigma_{k}^2$, then \mathbb{E}_{H_1}[\tau^{\text{ASN2T}}]\leq\mathbb{E}_{H_1}[\tau^{(p)}]+O\left(\frac{K^2}{r^2}(\log(1/\alpha))^{2/3}\right) ... Asymptotically, \lim_{\alpha\rightarrow0}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\tau^{\text{ASN2T}}]}{\log(1/\alpha)}\leq\lim_{\alpha\rightarrow0}\frac{\mathbb{E}[\tau^{(p)}]}{\log(1/\alpha)}.

results.notes: Comparative bound: only the additive term is in O(.), so notation 'exact' with the O term written without a constant; inexact. Corollary also states the asymptotic ratio comparison as alpha -> 0 (not recorded separately).
